0.0.n: Before a time word, ある introduces an unspecified occasion.

0.1.n: ある日 is a common way to begin a story.

0.3.n: 雷太 is the first part of the personal name 雷太郎, split across two tokens here.

0.4.n: 郎 completes the personal name 雷太郎; it is not a separate word here.

0.5.n: は marks Raitaro as the person the sentence is about.

0.6.n: Japanese nouns do not require separate singular and plural forms.

0.7.n: の links 山 to 奥, identifying which place has the interior being described.

0.8.n: 奥 refers to an inner or faraway part of a place.

0.9.n: へ marks the direction of movement and is pronounced like え.

0.10.n: 行きました is the polite past form of 行く.

1.0.n: ここではなく、そこで refers back to the mountain location; で marks where the meeting happened.

1.2.n: 不思議 describes something puzzling or unusual and takes な before a noun.

1.3.n: な connects the describing word 不思議 to the noun おじいさん.

1.4.n: おじいさん can mean grandfather, but here it refers to an elderly man who is not identified as family.

1.5.n: に marks the person someone meets when used with 会う.

1.6.n: 会いました is the polite past form of 会う; the person doing the meeting is understood from context.

2.1.n: お前 is a very informal address that can sound rough or superior, fitting the older speaker here.

2.2.n: に marks the person who will receive the teaching.

2.4.n: カエル is written in katakana, a common choice for animal names.

2.5.n: の links カエル to 術, describing what kind of technique it is.

2.6.n: 術 refers to a special technique or skill, potentially magical in this story.

2.7.n: を marks カエルの術 as what the speaker will teach.

2.8.n: 教えて plus やろう offers to teach as a favor, with a rough or superior tone.

0.lit: A certain day, as for Raitaro, toward the mountains’ interior went.
0.tip: 山の奥へ combines a place, its deep interior, and the direction particle へ.

1.lit: There, with a mysterious old man, met.
1.tip: Japanese often leaves out the subject when context makes it clear; here, Raitaro is still the subject.

2.lit: To you, the frog’s art, I shall teach as a favor.
2.tip: てやろう presents an intended action as a favor, but can sound condescending rather than polite.
